seo.metaTitle: Image to PDF Converter: JPG and PNG to One PDF
seo.metaDescription: Combine photos and scans into a single PDF in your browser. Reorder pages, choose A4 or fit to image, and nothing is ever uploaded.

intro: Turning photos into a PDF is one of those tasks that always seems to require uploading personal documents to a website you have never heard of. This converter does not. It writes the PDF file itself, inside your browser, using nothing but the images you choose. Add as many as you like, drag them into the right order, pick whether each page should match its image or fit onto A4, and download one PDF. It is the tool for a stack of phone photos of a signed contract, a passport and visa application, receipts for an expense claim, or a set of scans that a form insists on receiving as a single file. Your documents never leave the device, which for this particular job is not a small detail.
howto: Drop your images onto the box, or press Choose files. You can add several at once and come back and add more later.
Check the order in the list underneath. The arrows move a page up or down, and the cross removes one. The order in the list is the order in the PDF.

Choose the page size. Fit each page to its image keeps the exact shape of every photo. A4 or Letter places each image centred on a standard page with a margin, which is what most forms and printers expect.
Pick a quality. Balanced is right for almost everything. Use High for documents with small print, and Smaller file when there is an upload size limit.
Press Create PDF. The file downloads straight away and the size is shown so you know whether it fits whatever limit you are working to.
benefits: The privacy is the point. The usual advice for this task is to use one of the large online PDF sites, which means uploading your identity documents, bank statements or signed contracts to someone else's server and trusting a deletion policy you have not read. Here the PDF is assembled byte by byte in your browser: there is no upload, no queue, no account and no file sitting on a machine you do not control. You can load this page, turn off your internet connection, and it still works.

It is also more careful than it needs to be. Images are re-encoded to a baseline JPEG before being embedded, which keeps the output compatible with every PDF reader rather than only the forgiving ones, and transparency is flattened onto white instead of turning black, which is the usual result when a PNG with a transparent background is put into a PDF. Very large photos are scaled before drawing so a 48 megapixel phone picture does not silently produce a blank page on an iPhone.
useCases: Anyone dealing with an application form is the most common visitor: visa and passport applications, university admissions, job applications and bank paperwork all tend to demand a single PDF while people naturally have a folder of phone photos. Being able to order the pages before building matters here, since these forms usually specify a sequence.

It is equally useful for expense claims, for turning a set of receipts or invoices into one attachment, and for anyone digitising paper with a phone camera rather than a scanner. If the finished PDF is too large for an upload limit, dropping the quality setting is the fastest fix, and our [image compressor](/tools/image-compressor/) can shrink the photos further before you start.

faqs.a: No. The images are read by your browser and the PDF file is constructed on your device. Nothing is transmitted at any point, which is exactly why this tool is worth using for identity documents and contracts.

faqs.q: Can I choose the page order?
faqs.a: Yes. Every image appears in a list with arrows to move it up or down and a cross to remove it. The list order is the page order, so arrange it before pressing Create PDF.

faqs.q: Should I pick fit to image or A4?
faqs.a: Fit to image keeps every photo at its own shape and is best when the images are already the right proportions. A4 or Letter centres each image on a standard page with a margin, which is what to choose when the PDF will be printed or submitted to a form that expects standard pages.

faqs.q: Why is my PDF larger than the original photos?
faqs.a: It usually is not, but it can be if your originals were heavily compressed already, because they are re-encoded. Choosing Smaller file reduces it. Compressing the images first gives you the most control over the final size.

faqs.q: What happens to a PNG with a transparent background?
faqs.a: The transparent areas become white. PDF images embedded this way have no alpha channel, so the alternative would be for them to come out black, which is what happens in a lot of converters.

faqs.q: Can it merge existing PDF files?
faqs.a: No, this one takes images only. Merging PDFs means parsing and rewriting their internal structure, which is a different and much larger job than writing a new file from scratch.
